facts.statement: The type species of the genus Notochampsa is Notochampsa istedana.
Fossils of Notochampsa have been found in the lower Clarens Formation of the Karoo Supergroup in South Africa.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the lower Clarens Formation of the Karoo Supergroup in South Africa

facts.statement: Notochampsa lived during the Pliensbachian stage of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: dating back to the Pliensbachian stage of the Early Jurassic

facts.statement: The genus Notochampsa was named by Robert Broom in 1904.
facts.quote: The genus was named in a paper published in 1904 by Robert Broom.

facts.statement: A second species, Notochampsa longipes, was also described.
facts.quote: a second species, named N. longipes, was also described

facts.statement: In 1924, the species Notochampsa longipes was moved to its own genus, Erythrochampsa.
facts.quote: Later in 1924, N. longipes was given its own genus, Erythrochampsa.

facts.statement: Sidney Haughton created the family Notochampsidae to include Notochampsa.
facts.quote: Sidney Haughton created the family Notochampsidae for Notochampsa.

facts.statement: Notochampsa was historically used to include other protosuchian genera such as Dyoplax, Pedeticosaurus, Platyognathus, and Protosuchus.
facts.quote: Notochampsa was later used to include other genera of protosuchians such as Dyoplax, Pedeticosaurus, Platyognathus, and Protosuchus

facts.statement: Notochampsa was once assigned to the suborder Sphenosuchia.
facts.quote: Notochampsa had also once been assigned to the suborder Sphenosuchia.

facts.statement: A 2021 revision confirmed Notochampsa as a valid taxon, placing it as the sister group to Orthosuchus within the monophyletic family Notochampsidae.
facts.quote: A revision in 2021 found it valid taxon, and phylogenetic analysis recovered it as sister to Orthosuchus, in a monophyletic Notochampsidae.

facts.statement: Notochampsa lived between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to Pliensbachian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Pliensbachian (201.4 to 184.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Notochampsa is an extinct genus of protosuchian crocodyliform.
rejected.quote: Notochampsa is an extinct genus of protosuchian crocodyliform.

rejected.statement: Notochampsa is the youngest known occurrence of a crocodylomorph and vertebrate body fossil from the Karoo Basin of South Africa.
rejected.quote: Notochampsa comes from a period of relative fossil scarcity, and is the youngest known occurrence of a crocodylomorph (and vertebrate body fossil) from the Karoo Basin of South Africa.
